__comment: Combined per manager request: applications-monitor.json, nx-applications-dashboard.json, and nx-applications-monitoring.json all queried the same metric family (container_cpu/memory/network_*, kube_pod_container_status_ready/restarts) at three different granularities (fleet health / namespace-wide aggregate / per-service detail) - combined into one dashboard with those three as collapsible sections instead of three separate files, all sharing one $datasource + $namespace picker. BUGS FIXED while merging: (1) applications-monitor.json's Fleet Health panels queried an exact hardcoded snapshot of pod names including their ReplicaSet hash suffix (e.g. 'applications-archiver-789855dc6d-ngx9v') - those hashes change on every deploy, so this was already stale and would show 'Bad'/'No data' for current pods. Rebuilt as a dynamic label_values() query against $namespace, no hardcoded pod list. (2) nx-applications-dashboard.json's panels used gridPos w:30, exceeding Grafana's 24-column grid (always rendered clipped/overflowing), and its last two panels (Pod Count / Pod Restarts) overlapped by 2 grid units - re-tiled as a clean 2-column layout. (3) nx-applications-monitoring.json's 60 panels (15 services x 4 panels) had no row headers at all, just implicit grouping by title prefix - added one collapsible row divider per service for real navigability. | Folded in the 4 genuinely new panels from Application Health Executive View (Request Rate, Request Latency p95, HTTP Success Rate, Services Down by name) as a new top row - its other panels (Services Up count, Overall Fleet Health %, CPU Usage by Pod, Hourly Request Volume) duplicated what Fleet Health Summary / All-Pods Resource Overview already cover here, so those were not re-added. application-health-executive.json deleted as a duplicate.

panels.title: 🚦 Request Golden Signals & Down Services (folded in from Application Health Executive View)
Request Latency p95 by Service (where instrumented)
panels.description: http_request_duration_seconds is opt-in per service (pipeline-lib-go's shared HTTP metric set) - not every service installs it. Blank for a service means it hasn't wired up the shared HTTP metrics, not that it's slow.

panels.title: Services Down (instant)
panels.description: Any service currently reporting up == 0, named by job. The Fleet Health Summary row below gives you counts; this names which one.

panels.title: Pods Good vs Bad (count)
panels.description: Percentage of pods in the selected namespace that are Good (Ready) vs Bad (Not Ready)

targets.expr: count(min by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{namespace="$namespace", pod!~"grafana-dashboard.*"})) - sum(min by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{namespace="$namespace", pod!~"grafana-dashboard.*"}))

panels.title: Pods OK and Bad (count)
panels.description: Counts of pods in the selected namespace that are Ready (OK) vs Not Ready (Bad)

targets.expr: count(min by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{namespace="$namespace", pod!~"grafana-dashboard.*"})) - sum(min by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{namespace="$namespace", pod!~"grafana-dashboard.*"}))
